Syrian hamsters generally prefer paper-based bedding or aspen wood shavings. Paper bedding is popular because it's soft, holds burrows well, and is dust-free. Aspen is the only safe wood shaving—avoid cedar and pine entirely since the oils can cause respiratory problems. Some hamsters also like a mix with a little hay for nesting material.

That said, every hamster has individual preferences. Try offering a few options and see what yours likes to nest in and burrow through. Just make sure whatever you choose is at least 3-6 inches deep so they can create tunnels.

Is this for a new hamster, or are you trying to figure out what your current one prefers?

reply:
For sautéing vegetables, medium-high heat is generally the sweet spot. You want the pan hot enough to get a nice color without burning, but not so hot that everything goes up in smoke. The oil should shimmer when you add it, then add your veggies and spread them out in a single layer—don't overcrowd, or they'll steam instead of sauté.

If you're doing a quick stir-fry, high heat works. But for regular sautéing where you want to cook through and brown, stick with medium-medium high and keep the veggies moving.
